content:
From today, Spotify users in several countries can set up managed accounts for their children without a Premium subscription. Here are the details.

Managed accounts are available from today to parents and guardians with free Spotify accounts.

Managed accounts are a special type of Spotify account that allows parents to provide their children with an independent, age-appropriate listening experience, with parental controls. This feature was first launched in select countries in 2024 for Premium Family subscribers and has since rapidly expanded to more regions.

Through Spotify's managed accounts, parents can filter explicit content, block specific artists or songs, disable video features, and keep their children's listening history separate from their own recommendations. More importantly, children also get their own independent Spotify Wrapped.

Starting today, Spotify has removed the restriction that managed accounts are only available to Premium Family subscribers. This means any parent with a Spotify account can now set up a managed account for their children for free.

Spotify said the free managed account feature will first launch in the United States, United Kingdom, Australia, France, Germany, and the Netherlands, and will gradually expand to Europe, Latin America, and other countries.

To set up a managed account, parents can click "Add account" in the sidebar of the Spotify homepage, then select "Add an account for a child under 13." An introduction page will then appear, listing available features and monitoring options, allowing parents to decide whether to allow explicit content (filtering enabled by default) and video and Canvas content (filtering disabled by default).

Managed accounts are private and cannot be searched, using avatars instead of uploaded profile photos, and do not support messaging features. Children can still enjoy personalised playlists such as Daylist and Discover Weekly, and have their own Spotify Wrapped independent of their parent's or guardian's account.

Spotify also mentioned that managed accounts do not require children to have their own phone. Once a managed account is added to the main account, family members can easily switch between different accounts on a shared device, with the parent or guardian's account protected by a PIN code.

Spotify noted that managed accounts only apply to music, meaning children cannot access other content such as podcasts and audiobooks. The company added that it has been listening to feedback from parents and guardians to continuously improve the managed account feature.

Finally, when a child reaches the legal minimum age in their country, the managed account can be converted to a regular Spotify account. Before the user turns 18, the conversion process must be approved by a parent; after turning 18, they can decide for themselves whether to convert.
